status: frozen after identifying the untested disk-versus-bulge loophole and before inspecting any morphology-residual result
reopen_reason: The prior slab inversion used disk scale, surface brightness, gas fraction, and Hubble type but did not explicitly solve the different 3D fields of a thin disk and a vertically extended bulge. A constitutive theory makes a directional morphology prediction that can break the mass-only BTFR confound.
weak_field_system: div[epsilon(X) grad Phi] = 4 pi G rho_b
claim_boundary: This is an axisymmetric weak-field benchmark. Density-dependent permittivity and refracted gravity are prior art; a reciprocal covariant action and lensing prediction remain unproved.

solver.coordinates: cell-centered axisymmetric R>=0,z>=0 quadrant with reflection at R=0 and z=0

SPARC_inputs.residual_blindness: Morphology, component masses, and bulge scale are derived only from SPARC photometry and Vgas/Vdisk/Vbul baryonic component fields. Vobs is forbidden until the catalog and folds are frozen.

empirical_morphology_test.primary_target: whole-galaxy median residual in log10(gobs/gRAR_fixed) beyond 3 Rdisk
empirical_morphology_test.predicted_direction: At fixed baryonic controls, thinner and more disk-dominated systems receive a larger positive outer residual than bulge-dominated systems.
controls: Hubble type without explicit bulge geometry
matched disk-dominated and bulge-dominated systems in mass, size, gas fraction, and surface brightness

stop_rules: No per-galaxy permittivity, transition density, smoothing length, disk thickness, or bulge scale may be fitted to Vobs.
If morphology response changes sign over the allowed global parameter space, report the sign boundary instead of choosing a favorable region after seeing SPARC.
A galaxy morphology pass cannot establish cluster lensing or a covariant action.
If the empirical sign or permutation gate fails, NBP0-M1 is not supported even if selected synthetic parameter values produce attractive example curves.
